{{Short description|German-born biologist (1928–1991)}}

'''Aline Ehrlich''', née Buchbinder (26 December 1928 – 5 February 1991), was a German-born freshwater [[biologist]] and [[geologist]], recognized for her work on [[diatoms]]. She taught at the [[University of Paris]], and then worked for twenty years for the Geological Survey of Israel, compiling the ''Atlas of the Inland-water Diatom Flora of Israel'', which was published posthumously by the [[Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities]].

==Early life and education==
Ehrlich was born in [[Berlin]], Germany, on 26 December 1928.<ref name=":0" /> In 1938, when Ehrlich was ten, the family moved to hide from the [[Nazism|Nazis]] in a small southern French village during the German occupation.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Moshkovitz |first=Shimon |last2=Round |first2=Frank |date=May 1993 |title=OBITUARY: Dr Aline Ehrlich (1928–1991) |url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/0269249X.1993.9705255 |journal=Diatom Research |language=en |volume=8 |issue=1 |pages=221–225 |doi=10.1080/0269249X.1993.9705255 |issn=0269-249X|url-access=subscription }}</ref> She completed her secondary education in [[Pau, Pyrénées-Atlantiques|Pau]], France.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book |last=Haines |first=Catherine M.C. |date=2001 |title=International Women in Science |url=https://doi.org/10.5040/9798400671609 |doi=10.5040/9798400671609|publisher=ABC-CLIO|pages=92–93}}</ref> Ehrlich studied many subjects including [[chemistry]], [[geology]], [[botany]] and [[zoology]] at the [[University of Paris]]. It was at the university that Ehrlich developed her particular interest in diatoms.<ref name=":1" />

==Career==
Ehrlich taught in the geology department at the University of Paris, but in addition was also a high school biology teacher.<ref name=":0" /> In 1969 Ehrlich left her position with the Geological Department at the University of Paris and moved to Israel to work for [[the Geological Survey of Israel]], where she remained for 20 years. She had had a childhood dream of living in Jerusalem.<ref name=":0" /> Ehrlich investigated distributions of calcareous nannofossils across inland Israel, and their use in stratigraphy.<ref name=":0" /> She also co-authored bibliographies of work on the geology of [[Lebanon]] and  [[Syria]]. She compiled the ''Atlas of the Inland-water Diatom Flora of Israel'' before she died, although it was published posthumously, in 1995, by the Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities, in the Flora Palaestina series.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlas of the Inland-Water Diatom Flora of Israel |url=https://www.academy.ac.il/ShopEng/?nodeId=1534&author=Aline%20Ehrlich |access-date=5 April 2025 |website=Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities}}</ref>

Ehrlich was multi-lingual, speaking [[German language|German]], [[French language|French]], [[English language|English]], [[Russian language|Russian]] and [[Hebrew]].<ref name=":1" />

Ehrlich died in 1991 aged 63, “after a severe and long-lasting disease”.<ref name=":0" />
